display_name: List held authorizations — what is blocked on a role right now
description: R1 held-authorization queue (2026-08-17). Read-only answer to "what is blocked on <role>?" for a session with zero memory of a prior seat — a freshly-booted or freshly-rotated coordinator, an operator checking status, or any peer wondering why a request has gone quiet. Returns open entries (retired_at unset) by default; pass include_retired for the full history. Optional owed_by_role / requesting_peer filters compose with AND. Never filters or flags by age itself — this queue has no silent TTL by design (a queue that silently forgets is worse than no queue), so created_at is returned as-is and the caller judges staleness directly.
embedding_description: Checking whether any commit request is stuck waiting on a first-party authorization Git-Controller has not received yet, and who it is waiting on. The read a fresh session runs instead of scrolling a transcript to answer 'what's blocked on the coordinator' or 'what's blocked on Git-Controller'. Every entry carries when the refusal happened so staleness is visible, never hidden by an expiry timer.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: {"entries": [{entry_id, requesting_peer, owed_by_role, branch_or_request_ref, reason, created_at, retired_at, retired_reason, retired_by}, ...], "count": N}.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: An empty list is good news (nothing blocked) and should read as such. A non-empty list — especially one with an old created_at — is worth calling out plainly: name who is blocked and who it is waiting on, do not just report the count.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: A plain state read of held_authorization, filtered by the optional owed_by_role / requesting_peer and by retired_at IS NULL unless include_retired is set.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: state_service_unavailable: the state service is not bound.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: state_service_unavailable is worth a retry once the platform is up. This verb issues no writes and is always safe to retry.
